mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically from -16.3% to -12.0% over four weeks, indicating a consistent recovery trend. This upward momentum will persist over the next four weeks, driving RETAIL_REC further above baseline.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 4.3 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days, or reverses by more than 2 percentage points in any single week.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has recovered from -20.6% to -13.7% (7 percentage point gain in one week), signaling rapid return to office routines. This workplace reactivation drives weekday retail visits and sustains RETAIL_REC gains over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises more than 5 percentage points in a single week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 6.9 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES does not sustain above -15% in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines despite WORKPLACES recovery.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has risen from 1.3% to 4.7% over four weeks, indicating sustained essential-goods shopping. This baseline consumer activity primes retail visits; consumers already in mobility routines extend trips to retail-recreation venues, amplifying RETAIL_REC recovery.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds 3% and RETAIL_REC shows positive week-on-week change
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM falls below 2% or RETAIL_REC fails to improve despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining elevated, indicating no trip-chaining effect.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility remains severely depressed at -45.6%, indicating ongoing restrictions or behavioral avoidance of public transport. If TRANSIT does not recover above -40% in the next week, commuting barriers persist, constraining RETAIL_REC recovery to less than -10%.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -40% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -45.6% in t-0w, showing minimal recovery
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers above -35% within one week and RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises above -10%, contradicting the constraint hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has stabilized around -27% to -32% over four weeks, indicating outdoor recreation remains suppressed. Suppressed outdoor alternatives do not drive substitution to retail-recreation; instead, the persistent outdoor deficit signals continued mobility restrictions that cap RETAIL_REC gains.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -25% for all four weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS averaged -29.1% over four weeks with no recovery trend
failure_condition: PARKS recovers above -20% and RETAIL_REC simultaneously exceeds -8%, indicating restrictions have genuinely loosened.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from 7.9% to 5.7% over four weeks, indicating residents are spending less time at home. Combined with RETAIL_REC recovery, this signals a shift in activity distribution: residents are reallocating time from home to retail-recreation venues, sustaining the recovery momentum over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines below 6% and RETAIL_REC rises above -12%
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell 2.2 points while RETAIL_REC rose 4.3 points
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL rises above 7% or RETAIL_REC falls below -13% in the next four weeks, indicating residents are not reallocating to retail venues.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-July in Madrid marks peak summer tourism and vacation season. RETAIL_REC recovery from -16.3% to -12.0% reflects seasonal demand surge. This seasonal lift will accelerate RETAIL_REC gains over the next four weeks as summer holiday mobility peaks, driving the metric further above baseline.
evidence_refs: fact:Decision date is 2021-07-15, peak summer season in Madrid
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed -10% by end of August, or shows week-on-week decline in any of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility jointly signal commuting infrastructure reactivation. WORKPLACES rose 6.9 points and TRANSIT improved 5.1 points in the most recent week. When both signals strengthen together, retail-recreation venues benefit from increased foot traffic during commute windows, amplifying RETAIL_REC gains over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve by more than 4 points in the same week
failure_condition: Either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT reverses by more than 3 points in the next week, or RETAIL_REC fails to improve despite both signals strengthening.
